system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show multiple successful HTTP connections from WS-LMARTINS-01 to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080 during the review window, including connections at 13:30:58, 13:40:51, 13:43:21, 13:45:21, 13:50:28, 13:55:32, 14:00:10, 14:05:36, and 14:10:35 UTC. The intervals in these records are not uniformly five minutes.

At 14:10:35 UTC, the proxy recorded a successful CONNECT to updates.pixelforge-suite.com:443, and host telemetry attributes the corresponding proxy connection to the approved PixelForge pfupdater.exe process.

The earlier listed proxy connections are not attributed to a destination hostname or process in the supplied records, so their relationship to the identified PixelForge updater connection is not established.

At 14:11 UTC, DC-NWD-01 connected to WS-LMARTINS-01 on TCP port 135; shortly afterward, a WmiPrvSE.exe process on the workstation terminated. The records do not show what action, if any, that process performed.
WS-LMARTINS-01 made SMB connections to FILE-NWD-01 at 13:55 and 14:03 UTC, with each corresponding FILE-NWD-01 log recording ANONYMOUS LOGON. The accessed shares or resources are not shown.

known_telemetry_limitations: For the earlier proxy connections, the supplied records show connections to the proxy but do not provide the proxy CONNECT destination, requesting process, or TLS contents.
The supplied records do not include the WMI operation or command, the reason for the DC-to-workstation connection, or evidence establishing whether it was authorized.
The SMB records do not identify the accessed share or resource or explain why the server logged ANONYMOUS LOGON.
claims_not_established: That the repeated proxy connections before 14:10 were all made by pfupdater.exe or were all to updates.pixelforge-suite.com.
That the DC-to-workstation RPC/WMI activity was malicious or, alternatively, an authorized operation.
That the SMB activity involved unauthorized access, data transfer, or execution.
That any data was exfiltrated or that the workstation was compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve complete proxy logs for the review window, including CONNECT destinations, user agents, byte counts, and any available process attribution.
Collect workstation process creation, WMI, and remote-management telemetry around 14:11 UTC, plus corresponding DC-side logs, to identify the initiator and operation.
Review FILE-NWD-01 SMB share-access and authentication logs for the 13:55 and 14:03 connections to determine what was accessed and why the sessions were logged as anonymous.
Confirm with IT whether any approved activity explains the DC-to-workstation connection and the FILE-NWD-01 SMB sessions.
